result.message: Current game resource index. Inventory array indices are object IDs; startingRoom is the initial location.

Puzzles, parser and inventory

- Register every word before its said() handler; synonyms belong to the same word group so "get", "take" and "grab" share one number. said(1, ...) matches any word; 9999 accepts the rest of the line where the profile allows it. Handle the unknown-input case in the room with a useful hint rather than a generic refusal.
- Inventory items live in the OBJECT table with a starting room; get(item) moves it to the player (room 255), drop(item) leaves it in the current room, has(item) tests it. Keep item names short and concrete: "Medallion", "Data Card". The status inventory (Tab or a controller calling status()) lists carried items; with f13 set the player can select one and v25 receives its number, or 255 on cancel. Manhunter builds a whole puzzle on this: the barker gives you a look, and showing item 13 within eight seconds earns the prize.
- Puzzle shapes that recur: find the key object across rooms and use it at one place; a locked door with a visible hint about what opens it; an NPC who wants an item and gives another; a timed chase where the exit must be found before a counter ends; a skill game with a learnable rhythm; a maze whose walls are the control screen and whose reward is counted in flags (the demo pack's arcade maze collects twelve squares, each a flag). Chain them so each solved puzzle opens the next screen or unlocks a conversation.
- Fairness: every death should be foreshadowed by something the player can see or read; every essential item should be visible in the picture or named in a look description; every puzzle should have at least one in-world hint reachable by looking. The classics were unforgiving about walking dead states; avoid them or make the game warn.
- Points: add score with the scoring variable v3 on first completion of each step (guard with a flag), and set the maximum in v7 so the status line reads well. Small awards for looking and finding, larger ones for solving. Never write score awards into dialogue or print messages (e.g. do not print "(+10)" or "You earned 10 points"); the status line reports the score.
- Text economy: the parser reply that names the concrete object, action or consequence first reads best. Write the look description of a room as three to five sentences that mention every interactive object once.
- State discipline: one flag per world fact, one variable per counter, variables 32 and above for authored state. Inspect existing logic and bindings before allocating state; the supplied boilerplate uses ordinary IDs that you can change with coordinated edits to its callers and state. Record what each flag and variable means in the world bible as you introduce it.

Sprites, loops and cels

- set.view keeps the object's current loop when the new view has that many loops and otherwise takes loop 0; set.loop, set.loop.v and the automatic direction-driven loop change keep the current cel when the new loop has that many cels and otherwise take cel 0. Nothing resets to 0 on its own. To restart an animation from its first frame, call set.cel(o, 0) explicitly. Manhunter's knife game leans on this: it re-selects the barker's loop every cycle while waiting for his cel to come round.
- animate.obj(o) initialises the object; select view, loop, cel and position before draw(o). draw makes it visible and starts update processing; erase removes it and restores what was under it. stop.update(o) freezes a drawn object as scenery that no longer costs a redraw and no longer wipes text near it; start.update resumes.
- Four-loop views follow the direction table: loop 0 right, 1 left, 2 down, 3 up, chosen from the object's direction each step unless fix.loop holds it. Two- and three-loop views use loops 0 and 1 for right and left only. Mirror loops save bytes: the view format lets a loop mirror another.
- Cel width and height come from the cel; the object's baseline is its bottom row. Sprites clip at the screen edge and the interpreter clamps a placement that would leave the screen.
- end.of.loop(o, f) plays to the last cel and sets f; reverse.loop(o, f) plays back to cel 0. Both install a one-cycle delay before the first change, so a completion flag arrives one cycle later than a naive count suggests. Use them for doors, levers and gestures that must finish before the next step.
- Priority: an object takes the priority band of its baseline row (4 at the top, rising by one every twelve rows) unless set.priority fixes it. Scenery painted at a higher priority occludes the sprite; paint doorway frames and foreground rocks at the band above the floor they stand on. Priority 15 is drawn over everything and skips barrier and water checks, which is how cursors and floating labels behave.
- Scale the ego first. The classic hero is 6 to 10 pixels wide and 28 to 36 tall; doors, chairs and beds must fit that figure on the same baseline. Compose a frame with the real ego before drawing any other sprite.
- Two or three restrained environmental animations, a pennant, a drip, a blinking light, carry a room. Give each a readable phase pattern and a slow cycle.time. Crowds of tiny animations flicker at native resolution.

rooms.title: Precinct Front Desk
rooms.description: Prakash assigns Dana the pharmacy break-in; the duty board records the driver's name and the route to records and the street.

rooms.title: Records Office
rooms.description: Compare the delivery ledger with dispatch's logged route to expose the driver's false account; return to the desk to ask for reminders.

rooms.title: Millhaven Street
rooms.description: Bud watches the patrol car and points Dana toward the pharmacy and Pier Road; the street connects the district.

rooms.title: Pharmacy
rooms.description: Interview the frightened pharmacist, photograph the broken lock, and collect the marked bottle's evidence without losing its provenance.

rooms.title: Pier Road Warehouse
rooms.description: Link witness and records to the warehouse, call backup before entry, arrest the suspect and return to Prakash to file a complete report.

facts.name: protagonist
facts.text: Officer Dana Reyes is a rookie in a navy uniform and cap, carrying a badge and radio from the start.

facts.name: assignment
facts.text: Prakash issues the pharmacy break-in assignment once at the front desk; f40 means assigned, worth 10 points once.

facts.name: case score
facts.text: Maximum score v7 is 215: assignment 10, driver discrepancy 25, pharmacy documentation and evidence 30, warehouse connection 40, backed-up arrest 60, complete report 50. Guard every award with a persistent flag.

facts.name: clue chain
facts.text: Driver Ellis Vale claims a 9 PM pharmacy delivery. The duty board gives the time and his name; records and dispatch contradict his route; pharmacist and marked bottle connect his van to the warehouse on Pier Road.

facts.name: safety and procedure
facts.text: Bud warns before warehouse entry without backup. Evidence can always be revisited; Prakash explains missing elements of an incomplete report. The player can return to the precinct at any time.

facts.name: starting inventory
facts.text: Inventory item 0 badge and item 1 radio are carried at start. Neither is consumed. Badge confirms authority; radio contacts dispatch or backup.

quests.name: Get the assignment
quests.description: Talk to Sergeant Prakash at the front desk, then read the duty board for Ellis Vale's claimed 9 PM delivery and directions.

quests.name: Check the driver's story
quests.description: Compare the records ledger and dispatch's log with Vale's claimed pharmacy delivery.

quests.name: Document the break-in
quests.description: Interview the pharmacist, photograph the lock and preserve the marked bottle.

quests.name: Find the warehouse
quests.description: Connect the records, witness testimony and bottle to the warehouse on Pier Road.

quests.name: Arrest with backup
quests.description: Call for backup before entering the warehouse and arrest the suspect with evidence in hand.

quests.name: File the case
quests.description: Return to Prakash at the front desk and file a report covering the discrepancy, physical evidence and arrest.

commands.name: said
commands.help: Can match only when f2 is set, the parser count/error position is nonzero, and f4 is clear. Word ID 1 matches one word. Profile 2.089 requires an exact count and treats 9999 literally; later profiles use 9999 to accept the remaining tail, including a terminator-only recorded unknown token. Success sets f4. Matches registered parser word groups; operands are quoted vocabulary or word IDs, including wildcard 1 and tail 9999 where the profile supports it.

commands.name: set.horizon
commands.help: Set the horizon; nonexempt objects at or above it are placed at least one row below it.

commands.name: set.v
commands.help: Set the flag whose number is stored in the variable.

commands.name: reset.v
commands.help: Clear the flag whose number is stored in the variable.

commands.name: new.room
commands.help: Switch rooms immediately: copy old v0 to v1, set v0 to the destination, preserve ego's view in v16, set f5, reset transient room state, and end logic flow. Entry v2=1/2/3/4 places ego at Y=167/X=0/Y=37/X=160-width, then clears v2. Build-specific immediate destination aliases apply only when the selected profile defines them. Switches to a literal room number with room initialization semantics.

commands.name: position
commands.help: Set the object's current and previous position to immediate X and baseline Y. Places the left edge and bottom baseline at literal x,y; increasing sprite height extends upward.

commands.name: position.v
commands.help: Set the object's current and previous position from the X and baseline-Y variables. Places left edge and bottom baseline using x,y variable values.

commands.name: set.view
commands.help: Bind the loaded immediate view to the object. The current loop is kept when the view has that many loops (else loop 0), then the current cel when that loop has it (else cel 0). Selects a literal VIEW resource number, keeping an in-range loop and cel; artwork carries no animation timing or world position.

commands.name: set.view.v
commands.help: Bind the loaded view numbered by the variable to the object, keeping in-range loop and cel indices like set.view.

commands.name: set.loop
commands.help: Select the object's immediate loop; the current cel is kept when the loop has that many cels and otherwise becomes 0. Call set.cel to restart an animation. Selects a literal view loop and keeps the current cel when the loop has it; automatic direction selection may subsequently change the loop.

commands.name: set.loop.v
commands.help: Select the object's loop from the variable, keeping an in-range cel like set.loop.

commands.name: set.cel
commands.help: Select an immediate cel, refresh dimensions, clamp placement if needed, and remove the one-cycle animation delay. Selects a literal cel and clears the one-callback cycle delay.

commands.name: set.cel.v
commands.help: Select the cel numbered by the variable, refresh dimensions, clamp placement if needed, and remove the animation delay.

commands.name: set.priority
commands.help: Give the object the immediate fixed priority. Sets a literal priority and already fixes object depth. release.priority restores automatic baseline depth.

commands.name: set.priority.v
commands.help: Give the object the fixed priority stored in the variable. Sets fixed object depth from a variable value.
